high.title: Ibovespa falls with IPCA above expectations and US-Iran negotiations in focus; dollar falls to R$ 5.06
high.summary: The Ibovespa closed down 0.21% at 171,132.66 points despite positive momentum on Wall Street, as investors recalibrated bets on Brazil's next interest rate decision following new inflation data. While international markets were buoyed by expectations of a US-Iran agreement, Brazilian markets focused on domestic inflation concerns. The USD/BRL closed at R$ 5.0615, down 0.79% on the day and 1.86% for the week. Brazil's official IPCA inflation rose 0.58% in May (vs 0.67% in April) but accumulated 4.72% over 12 months - above the Central Bank's 3% target ceiling of 4.5%. This inflation overshoot is critical for FX and bond traders as it reduces the likelihood of aggressive Selic rate cuts and may pressure the BCB to maintain a more hawkish stance. The divergence between falling USD/BRL and rising inflation creates mixed signals for monetary policy, with markets now questioning the continuity of the easing cycle.

high.title: IPCA rises more than expected in May and accumulates 4.72% increase, above target
high.summary: Brazil's official IPCA inflation decelerated monthly to 0.58% in May from 0.67% in April, but came above market expectations of 0.55%. More critically, the 12-month accumulated inflation reached 4.72%, breaching the Central Bank's target ceiling of 4.5% (3% target with 1.5pp tolerance band). Market consensus had expected 4.68% annually. The main contributors were Food and beverages (+1.33% with 0.29pp impact), Housing (+1.22% with 0.18pp impact), and Health and personal care. This above-target inflation significantly impacts BCB monetary policy calculations and reduces scope for aggressive Selic cuts. For BRL traders, this reinforces expectations of higher-for-longer rates, potentially supporting the currency. Bond investors should expect continued yield pressure as markets price in a more hawkish BCB stance to bring inflation back within target range.

high.title: Treasury Direct today: rates fall at opening despite IPCA above expected; understand
high.summary: Brazilian government bond yields opened lower despite above-expected IPCA inflation, driven by reduced geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. The Treasury Prefixed 2029 fell from 14.60% to 14.53%, while IPCA+ 2050 dropped from IPCA + 7.20% to IPCA + 7.06%, and IPCA+ 2040 declined from IPCA + 7.51% to IPCA + 7.35%. The yield compression occurred as risk appetite improved following President Trump's decision to halt attacks against Iran and expectations of a memorandum of understanding being signed, potentially reopening the Strait of Hormuz within 30 days. This reduced fears of oil supply disruptions and further inflationary pressure. However, the disconnect between falling yields and rising domestic inflation may be temporary, as the above-target IPCA could force the BCB to maintain a more restrictive monetary stance, eventually pushing yields higher.

medium.title: Ibovespa reverses sign and rises with IPCA above ceiling and US-Iran agreement on radar; 5 things to know before investing today (12)
medium.summary: The Ibovespa opened negative after May inflation came above expected and exceeded the Central Bank's target ceiling, but reversed to positive territory during morning trading. The index initially fell 0.60% to 170,419.69 points but later gained 0.14% to 171,718.44 points. USD/BRL rose 0.08% to R$ 5.1055 despite the dollar weakening globally, with the DXY down 0.02%. US-Iran negotiation developments remained on investors' radar as a key market driver.

medium.title: IPCA + 8% in fixed income carries 'message between the lines': understand what's at stake
medium.summary: The Ibovespa has fallen about 15% from its near-200,000 point highs as markets question the continuity of Selic rate cuts. While Middle East conflicts contributed to inflationary pressure, Empiricus Research strategist Matheus Spiess argues Brazil's high interest rates primarily stem from domestic fiscal imbalances. The analyst suggests Brazil's structural fiscal problems are a key driver of the country's elevated interest rate environment, beyond external geopolitical factors.
